P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes. Residents may invoice non-residents (and expatriates) in foreign currency, and the proceeds must be paid into a Foreign Exchange Account (FEA) with a licensed bank (BoG Notice BG/GOV/SEC/2025/26). Pricing, invoicing or receiving foreign currency for goods or services from residents is prohibited: the cedi is the only legal tender. Inward remittances terminated into mobile-money wallets via payment service providers are paid out in cedis. Exporters must repatriate export proceeds (Foreign Exchange Act 2006, Act 723). For goods, under Letters of Commitment, the deadline is 120 days from shipment (BG/GOV/SEC/2025/34), with fines up to 5,000 penalty units and/or up to 10 years' imprisonment for unjustified non-repatriation.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Banks operate Foreign Exchange Accounts (FEA, credited with FX earnings/transfers) and Foreign Currency Accounts (FCA, FX cash). The BoG confirmed in 2025 that over-the-counter FX cash withdrawals from FEAs and FCAs are allowed, and cheques may be issued on them. Earnings from non-residents must go into an FEA (P1).

P4_paypal.question: Can residents receive money via PayPal?
P4_paypal.answer: No local PayPal. Ghana is absent from PayPal's official worldwide markets list (199 markets) and from PayPal's Payouts country table. A 2026 guide confirms a PayPal account cannot be created with Ghana as the country. Workarounds via foreign accounts or exchangers are not recommended (terms of service and exchange-control risk).

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Simplest form: a sole proprietorship (business name) registered with the Office of the Registrar of Companies (ORC). It costs GHS 130, with a mandatory annual renewal of GHS 70 (payable by USSD *222# or on ghana.gov.gh). Tax registration uses the Ghana Card PIN (L2). Note: under the new VAT Act every SERVICE provider must register for VAT within 30 days of starting (L4).

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: Since 1 April 2021 the Ghana Card Personal Identification Number (PIN) is the individual taxpayer identification number, replacing GRA-issued TINs (transition ended 31 Dec 2021). It is quoted on returns, tax payments and business registrations. Companies keep their own TINs.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: A resident's assessable income is worldwide income from all sources. 2026 annual bands for resident individuals (Income Tax (Amendment) Act 2026, Act 1178; GRA says effective 1 Sept 2026): first GHS 7,056 at 0%, then 5%, 10%, 17.5%, 25% and 30%, and 35% above GHS 600,000. Simplified regime (Modified Taxation Scheme) for informal-sector individuals: annual sales up to GHS 20,000 pay a fixed instalment (PTI). Sales of GHS 20,000–500,000 pay a flat 3% of turnover (PTT). Formally qualified professionals (lawyers, engineers, accountants) are excluded.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT Act 2025 (Act 1151), from 1 Jan 2026: 15% VAT plus 2.5% NHIL plus 2.5% GETFund, all on the price (effective 20%; COVID levy abolished; flat-rate scheme removed). Registration: suppliers of taxable SERVICES must register within 30 days of starting a taxable activity, with NO turnover threshold. Goods suppliers register above GHS 750,000. Exported services: consulting, professional, data-processing, information, advertising and IP-licensing services take place where the recipient uses them (s.42(2)). If used outside Ghana they are 'considered as exported' (s.42(4)), so no Ghana VAT is charged. But the Second Schedule's zero-rated services list covers only land and property abroad, IP for use abroad, and freight or transit items, not general services to foreign customers.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: Data Protection Act 2012 (Act 843). Every data controller that intends to process personal data must register with the Data Protection Commission, and an unregistered controller may not process personal data. Registration is renewed every two years. Processing needs the data subject's prior consent unless an exception applies, e.g. it is necessary for a contract with them.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Electronic Transactions Act 2008 (Act 772), s.49: consumers may cancel within 14 days of receiving goods, or within 7 days of concluding a services agreement, without reason or penalty. The only charge allowed is the direct cost of returning goods. Exceptions include unsealed audio or video recordings or computer software. A general Consumer Protection Bill has been pending since 2014 and was not enacted as of 2025.

L7_incentives.question: Legal incentives / tax holidays / special zones relevant to small digital businesses
L7_incentives.answer: (1) Modified Taxation Scheme: a flat 3% of turnover for annual sales of GHS 20,000–500,000, or fixed instalments below GHS 20,000, instead of full bookkeeping. (2) A 0% band on the first GHS 7,056 of annual chargeable income (2026). (3) Paystack Starter lets unregistered sellers collect up to GHS 30,000 before formalising. (4) The VAT reform removed cascading levies (effective 20%) and lets NHIL and GETFund be deducted as input tax by registered businesses. No digital-specific tax holiday for individuals was verified.

D1_id_document.question: Identity documents residents use for KYC (gateways, banks, platforms)
D1_id_document.answer: The Ghana Card (National Identification Authority). From 1 July 2022 it is the ONLY identification card accepted for transactions at all Bank of Ghana-licensed financial institutions: banks, payment service providers, forex bureaus and others. Ghanaians abroad without access to it may use passports. Its PIN is also the tax ID (L2). NIA registration officials are stationed at GRA offices.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: PayPal is not available; Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Card payments on your own site through Paystack (a Stripe company). Stripe lists this country under its extended network. (6) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. (7) Local official channel: Payments from non-residents must go into a Foreign Exchange Account (FEA) at a licensed bank (Bank of Ghana notice) (P1/P2). Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
